Marta —

Appreciate the request. High level answers below; I attached a concise attestation document and a current pinning matrix for reference. If helpful we can follow with a short walkthrough.

1) Provenance attestation:
- We record the model source (repository URL, commit/tag), license text + SPDX identifier, and a content checksum (SHA-256) at the time the model is onboarded to the catalog.
- For derived or fine-tuned artifacts we store parent-model references and the training-data provenance summary (metadata only; no raw data).
- We produce a one-page attestation (PDF) per catalog entry including: source URL, author, license, SBOM-like file list, and a cryptographic digest. See attached redwood_attestation_workflow_v1.pdf.

2) Version pinning mechanics and immutability:
- Pins are recorded as catalog facts and include: model_id, pinned_version, pin_author, timestamp, and rationale.
- By default pins are treated as immutable records: we do not silently repoint a pin. Any change to a pin creates a new pin entry and is audit-logged.
- We provide two pin styles: operational pins (soft pins) used by customers that can be updated by their org admins, and platform pins (hard pins) set by our catalog governance which require a documented change request + approval.

3) Rollback / unpin protocol (summary):
- If a supply-chain event occurs (license revocation, security issue), we trigger a catalog advisory and notify impacted customers by their subscribed contact.
- Customers on soft pins: we recommend immediate upgrade or manual repin; we can assist with migration bundles.
- Platform hard pins: changes go through our emergency unpin flow — a documented request, dual-owner approval, automated audit ledger entry, and an automated compatibility check before applying. See pinned rollback runbook (attached).

Attachments: redwood_attestation_workflow_v1.pdf, pinning_matrix_v3.xlsx, rollback_runbook.odt

I copied Laura (policy) and Priyom (supply-chain) for any technical or governance clarifications. We can deliver a signed attestation if you need a DocuSign flow.

Marta / Globex team —

Thanks for the thoughtful questions. A couple of technical clarifications to accompany Avery's response and the attachments:

- Compatibility check: our rollback gate runs a regression harness that includes tokenization equivalence, per-layer output-statistics (summary telemetry), and a customer-provided eval slice if requested. The gate fails if top-1 generation divergence exceeds configurable thresholds tied to the pinned model's SLA tier.
- Immutable pin semantics: when a platform hard pin is superseded we create an explicit 'deprecation' record that references the new pin, reason, and timeline for forced migration (if any). That record and the prior pin are both immutable ledger entries.
- Signed attestations: we can produce attestation PDFs both unsigned and PGP-signed; DocuSign is available for legal acceptance workflows.

Next steps: I'll attach a short example compatibility report and can run a demo of the rollback gate on your sample model if you provide the restricted metadata (no raw data needed).

Regards,

Supply-Chain Engineer
